sn47.35:3.2: This is the closest thing in the Suttas to the modern meditative practices known as “bare awareness”. Here, this meditative practice is said to be the “awareness” part of “mindfulness and awareness” (_satisampajañña_), as an complement to situational awareness in daily activities ([sn47.2]()). At [dn33:1.11.37]() = [an4.41:4.1]() it is a further development of immersion leading to mindfulness and awareness, at [an7.38:1.6]() and [an7.39:1.6]() it leads to the four kinds of textual analysis, and at [mn123:22.2]() it is one of the marvelous qualities of the Buddha.
